items.followUp: What is a hyperlink in HTML?

rubric.why: Identifies an anchor as a clickable link.
rubric.description: Identifies the purpose of an anchor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an anchor is a clickable link.

rubric.why: Names the HTML tag or attribute used to create an anchor.
rubric.description: Names the HTML anchor tag or its link attribute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving <a> or href.

modelAnswer: An anchor is a clickable text or image that links to another web page or a location on the same page.
In HTML, the <a> tag is used to create an anchor; the href attribute specifies the destination.

items.followUp: Describe star topology and state one advantage.

rubric.why: Describes the shared main cable and devices connected to it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that all computers/devices connect to one main cable and 1 mark for describing how data travels along that cable.

rubric.why: Describes the ring arrangement and data transmission between connected computers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that computers form a closed loop and 1 mark for describing data passing from one computer to the next around the ring.

modelAnswer: In a bus topology, all computers are connected to one main cable called the bus.
Data travels along this cable, and the intended computer receives it.
In a ring topology, each computer is connected to two other computers, forming a closed loop.
Data passes from one computer to the next around the ring until it reaches its destination.

items.followUp: How can an algorithm be tested using valid test data?

rubric.why: Recognizes that invalid test data does not meet the input requirements.
rubric.description: States what invalid test data is.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it is data outside the allowed range, of the wrong type, or otherwise unacceptable.

rubric.why: States that the test checks whether the algorithm handles unacceptable input appropriately.
rubric.description: Explains what the invalid-data test checks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the algorithm should reject the data or report an error.

modelAnswer: Enter data that does not meet the input requirements, such as a value outside the allowed range or the wrong data type.
Check that the algorithm rejects it or displays an appropriate error message.

rubric.why: Identifies absent test data as missing or unprovided input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that no input data is supplied or that required input is missing.

rubric.why: Explains that testing checks the algorithm's response to missing input.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that the algorithm should handle missing input appropriately, for example by prompting for input or displaying an error.

modelAnswer: Absent test data is a test in which no data is supplied for an input, or required input is missing.
It is used to check that the algorithm handles missing input appropriately, such as by prompting the user or displaying an error.

items.followUp: Explain the step-by-step strategy for solving a problem.

rubric.why: Identifies that the strategy represents the problem visually.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that the problem is represented using a picture or diagram.

rubric.why: Explains how a visual representation helps with understanding or solving the problem.
rubric.description: States the purpose of the strategy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the picture helps understand the problem, show relationships, or work out a solution.

modelAnswer: The “Draw a picture” strategy represents a problem visually using a picture or diagram.
The picture helps us understand the problem, see relationships between its parts, and work towards a solution.

items.followUp: Write two advantages of using pseudocode.

rubric.why: Identifies that a flowchart makes the logic or steps easier to understand.
rubric.description: Gives one advantage of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid advantage, such as making the steps easy to understand.

rubric.why: Identifies another valid advantage, such as communication, error detection, or program planning.
rubric.description: Gives a second advantage of a flowchart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different valid advantage.

modelAnswer: A flowchart presents the steps of a solution visually, making them easier to understand.
It helps communicate the solution and can make errors easier to find before programming.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <head> tag in HTML?

rubric.why: Identifies the body as the section containing content shown on the web page.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains the visible or displayed page content.

rubric.why: Identifies the body tag as the container for that page content.
rubric.description: Explains how the body tag is used.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the page content is placed between the opening and closing body tags.

modelAnswer: The <body> tag contains the content of an HTML page that is displayed in the browser, such as text and images.
This content is written between the opening <body> and closing </body> tags.
